Great question. I think many people already know this but here's my two cents:

Good UX does not bring people, but bad UX drive people away

Or to be precise, if the UX does not align well with the content they are looking, it can drive people away. Some of the cases here is voat alternatives, snapzu.com and stacksity.com. Let's talk about stacksity.com first because it has many differences with voat/reddit.

Stacksity use different approach. It does not display the subverse (or tags or $tags) on every page. In voat you have my subverses on top left and top menu that can be either default subs or my subverses. It's easier for navigation and filtering by subverse. Stacksity does not support that, so people who likes easier navigation will choose voat over stacksity. In voat, you see thumbnail and title of posts, around 20-30 posts each page, or 5-7 posts on screen. Stacksity using 9gag's format, showing large image for every post, showing around 1-2 posts each screen and using lazy loading. Stacksity is easier to enjoy image/video but harder for textual news and discussion. Voat is better at this area.

snapzu follows voat's format, with more complicated filtering. What is category? What is types? And after both of them there is tribes (subverse)? Moreover same with stacksity, they don't show my subverses (my tribes) on front page, which is a huge minus for navigation.

Familiarity is another point in UX. A discussion forum must have "reply/comment" features. Menu on top page. User panel on top right. Blog shows author, post date and user can comment on them. Voat users already familiar with reddit so they don't have trouble migrating. People don't like to learn new things for something that don't generate revenue.

That being said, the point is the UX may not fancy (animated text, good style, etc) but sufficient to user's need (navigation, mobile friendly, familiar).

Egg and chicken problem

Every content-oriented site like voat has the same egg/chicken problem. People don't want to post content when there aren't any users here. People don't want to become users when there aren't any content to begin with. Joel Spolsky write this topic well on this blog and I recommend you to read it.
